  );

  for delete
  using (author_id = auth.uid());

-- ==========================

create policy comment_select_visible
  on public.comments
  for select
  using (
    exists (
      select 1
      from public.posts p
      where p.id = comments.post_id
        and (
          (p.published_at <= now()
           and (p.unpublish_at is null or p.unpublish_at > now()))
          or p.author_id = auth.uid()
        )
    )
  );

  on public.comments
  for insert
  with check (
    author_id = auth.uid()
    and exists (
      select 1
      from public.posts p
      where p.id = comments.post_id
        and p.published_at <= now()
        and (p.unpublish_at is null or p.unpublish_at > now())

  );

  on public.comments

    or exists (
      select 1
      from public.posts p
      where p.id = comments.post_id

    )
  );

$$;

-- Helper function to determine if a user is an agent
create or replace function public.is_agent(u uuid)
returns boolean
language sql
stable
as $$
  select exists (
    select 1
    from public.profiles p
    where p.id = u and p.is_agent = true
  );
$$;

-- ==========================
-- Profiles table policies
-- ==========================

-- R1: Users read own profile; agents read any profile
create policy "profiles_select_self_or_agents"
  on public.profiles
  for select
  using ( id = auth.uid() OR public.is_agent(auth.uid()) );

-- R2: Users can update only their own display_name; is_agent must stay unchanged
create policy "profiles_update_own_display_name"
  on public.profiles
  for update
  using ( id = auth.uid() )
  with check ( is_agent = old.is_agent );

-- No insert/delete policies – only the service_role (bypasses RLS) can perform those actions


-- ==========================
-- Tickets table policies
-- ==========================

-- R3: Users read own tickets; agents read any ticket
create policy "tickets_select_self_or_agents"
  on public.tickets
  for select
  using ( requester_id = auth.uid() OR public.is_agent(auth.uid()) );

-- R4: Customers (any signed‑in user) can insert tickets only as themselves,
--     with status = 'open' and no assigned_agent
create policy "tickets_insert_self_open"
  on public.tickets
  for insert
  with check (
    requester_id = auth.uid()
    and status = 'open'
    and assigned_agent IS NULL
  );

-- R5: Agents can update any ticket; customers have no update rights
create policy "tickets_update_by_agents"
  on public.tickets
  for update
  using ( public.is_agent(auth.uid()) )
  with check ( true );

-- No delete policy – deletes are blocked for all non‑service_role users


-- ==========================
-- Grants / Revokes
-- ==========================

-- Authenticated users get the base privileges; RLS will restrict rows

-- Enable row level security on the storage objects table
alter table storage.objects enable row level security;

-- Helper functions ---------------------------------------------------------

-- Returns true for objects that are public (media bucket, path <uid>/public/...)
create or replace function public_media_object(o storage.objects)
returns boolean
language sql
stable
as $$
  select
    o.bucket_id = 'media' and
    o.name ~ '^[0-9a-fA-F-]{36}/public/.*$';
$$;

-- Returns true for objects that belong to the calling user (media bucket, path starts with uid/)
create or replace function own_media_object(o storage.objects)
returns boolean
language sql
stable
as $$
  select
    o.bucket_id = 'media' and
    o.name like auth.uid() || '/%';
$$;

-- Policies ---------------------------------------------------------------

-- R1: Anyone (anon & authenticated) can read public objects
create policy "public_media_read"
  on storage.objects
  for select
  to public
  using (public_media_object(storage.objects));

-- R2: Authenticated users can read everything in their own folder
create policy "own_media_read"
  on storage.objects
  for select
  to authenticated
  using (own_media_object(storage.objects));

-- R3: Authenticated users can insert objects only inside their own folder
create policy "own_media_insert"
  on storage.objects
  for insert
  to authenticated
  using (
    bucket_id = 'media' and
    name like auth.uid() || '/%'            -- path must start with their uid
  )
  with check (
    bucket_id = 'media' and
    name like auth.uid() || '/%' and
    owner = auth.uid()                      -- owner forced to caller
  );

-- R3: Authenticated users can update (rename/move) only objects they own and stay inside their folder
create policy "own_media_update"
  on storage.objects
  for update
  to authenticated
  using (
    bucket_id = 'media' and
    name like auth.uid() || '/%' and
    owner = auth.uid()
  )
  with check (
    bucket_id = 'media' and
    name like auth.uid() || '/%' and
    owner = auth.uid()
  );

-- R3: Authenticated users can delete only objects they own inside their folder
create policy "own_media_delete"
  on storage.objects
  for delete
  to authenticated
  using (
    bucket_id = 'media' and
    name like auth.uid() || '/%' and
    owner = auth.uid()
  );

-- R4: No policies grant access to the internal bucket or to media objects
-- that are not under a user’s folder, so they remain invisible to anon/auth.
-- Service role bypasses RLS automatically.

-- Grants (optional, ensures basic privileges are present) -----------------
grant select, insert, update, delete on storage.objects to authenticated, anon;

-- Helper function: check librarian status
create or replace function public.is_librarian(p_uid uuid)
returns boolean
language sql
stable
as $$
  select exists (
    select 1
    from public.librarians
    where user_id = p_uid
  );
$$;

-- Helper function: borrowing eligibility
create or replace function public.can_borrow(p_book_id bigint, p_uid uuid)
returns boolean
language plpgsql
stable
as $$
declare
  v_active_loans int;
  v_book_copies int;
  v_user_active_loans int;
begin
  -- active loans for the book
  select count(*) into v_active_loans
  from public.loans
  where book_id = p_book_id
    and returned_on is null;

  -- total copies of the book
  select copies into v_book_copies
  from public.books
  where id = p_book_id;

  if v_active_loans >= v_book_copies then
    return false;
  end if;

  -- active loans for the user
  select count(*) into v_user_active_loans
  from public.loans
  where borrower_id = p_uid
    and returned_on is null;

  return v_user_active_loans < 3;
end;
$$;

-- Enable Row Level Security on the api_keys table
alter table public.api_keys enable row level security;

-- -------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Policies
-- -------------------------------------------------------------------

-- R1: Authenticated users can SELECT only their own rows
create policy "select_own_keys"
    on public.api_keys
    for select
    using (auth.role() = 'authenticated' and user_id = auth.uid());

-- R2: Authenticated users can UPDATE (revoke) only their own active keys
create policy "revoke_own_key"
    on public.api_keys
    for update
    using (auth.role() = 'authenticated' and user_id = auth.uid() and revoked_at is null);

-- No INSERT or DELETE policies → users cannot create or delete keys (R3, R4)

-- -------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Helper trigger to enforce that only revoked_at may be changed
-- -------------------------------------------------------------------
create or replace function public.enforce_key_revocation()
returns trigger language plpgsql as $$
begin
    -- Ensure only the revoked_at column is being modified
    if (new.id         is distinct from old.id         or
        new.user_id    is distinct from old.user_id    or
        new.name       is distinct from old.name       or
        new.key_hash   is distinct from old.key_hash   or
        new.last4      is distinct from old.last4      or
        new.created_at is distinct from old.created_at) then
        raise exception 'Only revoked_at may be updated';
    end if;

    -- revoked_at must transition from NULL to a non‑NULL value
    if (old.revoked_at is not null) then
        raise exception 'A revoked key cannot be modified';
    end if;
    if (new.revoked_at is null) then
        raise exception 'revoked_at must be set to a non‑NULL timestamp to revoke';
    end if;

    return new;
end;
$$;

create trigger trg_enforce_key_revocation
    before update on public.api_keys
    for each row
    execute function public.enforce_key_revocation();

-- -------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Secure view exposing only allowed columns (excludes key_hash)
-- -------------------------------------------------------------------
create view public.api_keys_view
    security_barrier
as
select
    id,
    name,
    last4,
    created_at,
    revoked_at
from public.api_keys;

-- Column‑level privilege tightening

revoke select (key_hash) on public.api_keys from public;

-- Optionally, remove all direct SELECT rights on the table for non‑service roles
revoke select on public.api_keys from authenticated, anon;

    where id = p_folder
    union all

    from public.folders f
    join ancestors a on f.id = a.parent_id

    from ancestors a
    join public.folder_grants g on g.folder_id = a.id
    where g.user_id = p_user

  );

as $$
  select exists (

    where elem ->> 'method' = 'sso/saml'
  );

-- orgs policies

-- R1: members can see their orgs (SSO check)
create policy "orgs_select_member"
  on public.orgs
  for select
  using (
    exists (
      select 1
      from public.org_members om
      where om.org_id = orgs.id
        and om.user_id = auth.uid()
    )
    and ( (not orgs.require_sso) or public.is_sso_session() )
  );

-- R3: admins can update org settings (SSO check)

  on public.orgs
  for update
  using (
    exists (
      select 1
      from public.org_members om
      where om.org_id = orgs.id
        and om.user_id = auth.uid()
        and om.role = 'admin'
    )
    and ( (not orgs.require_sso) or public.is_sso_session() )

-- Enable Row Level Security
alter table public.items enable row level security;
alter table public.claims enable row level security;

-- ==========================
-- Items policies
-- ==========================

-- R1: Authenticated users can read all items
create policy items_select_all on public.items
  for select
  using (auth.role() = 'authenticated');

-- R1: Authenticated users can insert their own items (status forced to 'open')
create policy items_insert_self on public.items
  for insert
  with check (
    auth.uid() = found_by
    and new.status = 'open'
  );

-- R1: Finder can update only their own items (cannot change finder, can change status)
create policy items_update_self on public.items
  for update
  using (found_by = auth.uid())
  with check (
    new.found_by = old.found_by
    and new.status in ('open','claimed')
  );

-- ==========================
-- Helper function for claims
-- ==========================
create or replace function public.claim_one_approved_allowed(p_claim_id bigint, p_item_id bigint)
returns boolean
language plpgsql
security definer
as $$
begin
  return not exists (
    select 1
    from public.claims c
    where c.item_id = p_item_id
      and c.status = 'approved'
      and c.id <> p_claim_id
  );
end;
$$;

-- ==========================
-- Claims policies
-- ==========================

-- R2: Claimants see their own claims; finders see claims on their items
create policy claims_select_access on public.claims
  for select
  using (
    claimant_id = auth.uid()
    or item_id in (
      select i.id
      from public.items i
      where i.found_by = auth.uid()
    )
  );

-- R3: Authenticated users can create a claim on an open item they did NOT find
create policy claims_insert_self on public.claims
  for insert
  with check (
    auth.uid() = claimant_id
    and new.status = 'pending'
    and new.item_id in (
      select i.id
      from public.items i
      where i.status = 'open'
        and i.found_by <> auth.uid()
    )
  );

-- R4: Only the finder can approve/reject a pending claim on their item.
--     No other columns may change. At most one approved claim per item.
create policy claims_update_by_finder on public.claims
  for update
  using (
    item_id in (
      select i.id
      from public.items i
      where i.found_by = auth.uid()
    )
  )
  with check (
    -- immutable columns
    new.id = old.id
    and new.item_id = old.item_id
    and new.claimant_id = old.claimant_id
    and new.message = old.message
    -- status transition
    and old.status = 'pending'
    and new.status in ('approved','rejected')
    -- only one approved claim per item
    and (
      new.status = 'rejected'
      or public.claim_one_approved_allowed(old.id, old.item_id)
    )
  );

-- No delete policies (default deny)

-- ==========================
-- Grants (optional, ensure policies are visible)
-- ==========================
grant usage on schema public to anon, authenticated;
grant select, insert, update on public.items to authenticated;
grant select, insert, update on public.claims to authenticated;

-- ==========================
-- Items policies
-- ==========================
create policy "items_select_authenticated"
  on public.items
  for select
  to authenticated
  using (true);

create policy "items_insert_finder"
  on public.items
  for insert
  to authenticated
  with check (found_by = auth.uid());

create policy "items_update_finder"
  on public.items
  for update
  to authenticated
  using (found_by = auth.uid())
  with check (found_by = auth.uid());

-- Claims helper function (select)
-- ==========================
create or replace function public.claims_select_allowed(c public.claims)
returns boolean
language sql
stable
as $$
  select
    c.claimant_id = auth.uid()
    or exists (
      select 1
      from public.items i
      where i.id = c.item_id
        and i.found_by = auth.uid()
    );
$$;

-- ==========================
-- Claims policies
-- ==========================
create policy "claims_select_allowed"
  on public.claims
  for select
  to authenticated
  using (public.claims_select_allowed(claims));

create policy "claims_insert_allowed"
  on public.claims
  for insert
  to authenticated
  with check (
    claimant_id = auth.uid()
    and status = 'pending'
    and exists (
      select 1
      from public.items i
      where i.id = item_id
        and i.status = 'open'
        and i.found_by <> auth.uid()
    )
  );

create policy "claims_update_finder"
  on public.claims
  for update
  to authenticated
  using (
    exists (
      select 1
      from public.items i
      where i.id = claims.item_id
        and i.found_by = auth.uid()
    )
  );

-- ==========================
-- Trigger to enforce claim business rules
-- ==========================
create or replace function public.enforce_claim_rules()
returns trigger
language plpgsql
as $$
begin
  if tg_op = 'UPDATE' then
    -- only status may change
    if new.claimant_id <> old.claimant_id
       or new.item_id      <> old.item_id
       or new.message      <> old.message then
      raise exception 'Only the status field of a claim may be modified.';
    end if;

    -- can only modify pending claims
    if old.status <> 'pending' then
      raise exception 'Only pending claims can be approved or rejected.';
    end if;

    -- new status must be approved or rejected
    if new.status not in ('approved','rejected') then
      raise exception 'Status can only be set to approved or rejected.';
    end if;

    -- enforce at most one approved claim per item
    if new.status = 'approved' then
      if exists (
        select 1
        from public.claims c
        where c.item_id = new.item_id
          and c.status = 'approved'
          and c.id <> new.id
      ) then
        raise exception 'An approved claim already exists for this item.';
      end if;
    end if;
  end if;

  return new;
end;
$$;

create trigger trg_enforce_claim_rules
  before update on public.claims
  for each row
  execute function public.enforce_claim_rules();

-- ==========================
-- Revoke public privileges (optional safety)
-- ==========================
revoke all on public.items from public;
revoke all on public.claims from public;

    on public.care_team
    for select
    using (auth.uid() = doctor_id);

-- Lab Results table policies

    on public.lab_results
    for select
    using (
        -- Patient sees only released results
        (auth.uid() = (
              select user_id
              from public.patients
              where id = patient_id
         ) and released_at IS NOT NULL and released_at <= now())
        OR
        -- Doctor in care team sees all results
        (auth.uid() IN (

              from public.care_team
              where patient_id = patient_id
         ))
    );

create policy "lab_results_insert_doctor"
    on public.lab_results

-- Helper functions
create or replace function public.fn_can_book(p_user_id uuid, p_desk_id bigint, p_day date)
returns boolean
language sql
stable
as $$
    with m as (
        select tier, valid_until
        from public.memberships
        where user_id = p_user_id
    ),
    d as (
        select zone
        from public.desks
        where id = p_desk_id
    )
    select
        -- membership must exist
        exists (select 1 from m) and
        -- booking day must be today or later and not beyond membership validity
        p_day >= current_date and p_day <= (select valid_until from m) and
        -- tier must match desk zone (premium desks require premium tier)
        ( (select zone from d) = 'premium' and (select tier from m) = 'premium' )
        or
        ( (select zone from d) <> 'premium' )
$$;

create or replace function public.fn_upcoming_bookings(p_user_id uuid)
returns int
language sql
stable
as $$
    select count(*)
    from public.bookings
    where user_id = p_user_id
      and day >= current_date

    on public.desks

    on public.bookings
    for select
    to authenticated

  on public.proposals
  for select
  using (
    auth.role() = 'authenticated' and (
      speaker_id = auth.uid()
      or public.is_reviewer(auth.uid())
    )
  );

-- R2: Authenticated speakers can insert their own proposals, always as 'submitted'
create policy "proposals_insert"
  on public.proposals
  for insert
  with check (
    auth.role() = 'authenticated'
    and speaker_id = auth.uid()
    and coalesce(status, 'submitted') = 'submitted'
  );

-- R2: Speakers can update their own proposals while status is 'submitted' (cannot change status)
create policy "proposals_update_own_while_submitted"
  on public.proposals
  for update
  using (
    auth.role() = 'authenticated'
    and speaker_id = auth.uid()
    and status = 'submitted'
  )
  with check (
    status = 'submitted'  -- forbid status changes
  );

  on public.reviews
  for select
  using (

      reviewer_id = auth.uid()
      or (
        exists (
          select 1
          from public.proposals p
          where p.id = reviews.proposal_id
            and p.speaker_id = auth.uid()
            and p.status <> 'submitted'   -- decision made
        )
      )
    )
  );

    and reviewer_id = auth.uid()
    and public.is_reviewer(auth.uid())
